title: Video image recognition by the jumping spider, Maevia inclemens (Araneae: Salticidae)
why: It is the only source cited for a jumping spider flicker-fusion figure (about 40 Hz, known here only through Tan et al. 2023), which would set the view's pace.

title: Spectral sensitivity in jumping spiders (Araneae, Salticidae)
why: Its ERG spectra (330 to 700 nm in Maevia inclemens, known here through Lietzenmayer et al. 2019) would show how far into red the front eyes sense and whether more than two classes appear.

authors: Komiya M, Yamashita S, Tateda H
title: Turning reactions to real and apparent motion stimuli in the posterolateral eyes of jumping spiders
why: Apparent-motion timing in the rear side eyes would give the temporal resolution of the motion surround, which no opened source measures.

title: Movement detection in the posterolateral eyes of jumping spiders (Evarcha arcuata, Salticidae)
why: Speed and size thresholds of the rear side eyes would set the surround's motion detector and its timing.

authors: Steck M, Hanscom SJ, Iwanicki T, Sung JY, Outomuro D, Morehouse NI, Porter ML
title: Secondary not subordinate: opsin localization suggests possibility for color sensitivity in salticid secondary eyes
why: The full text would say which species and which secondary eyes carry a blue opsin, and so whether the monochrome surround is false for Menemerus bivittatus, the Gray Wall Jumping Spider.

title: Visual perception in jumping spiders (Araneae, Salticidae)
journal: PhD thesis, University of Canterbury (chapters 4 and 6)
why: Its chapters on retinal scanning and depth (a failed replication of the red-light depth result and evidence for accommodation) could not be read past page 32 here and would decide the distance row.

title: Saccadic tracking of targets mediated by the anterior-lateral eyes of jumping spiders
why: Latencies, speeds and accuracy of saccades driven by the front side eyes would set the gaze controller's jump.

authors: Menda G, Shamble PS, Nitzany EI, Golden JR, Hoy RR
title: Visual perception in the brain of a jumping spider
why: Brain recordings would show whether single neurons combine principal-eye and secondary-eye input, the question of how the eyes come together.

authors: Winsor AM, Remage-Healey L, Hoy RR, Jakob EM
title: Visual attention and processing in jumping spiders
why: A current review of attention and the hand-off between eyes would check the gaze rules against work this sheet could not open.

authors: Cerveira AM, Nelson XJ, Jackson RR
title: Spatial acuity-sensitivity trade-off in the principal eyes of a jumping spider: possible adaptations to a 'blended' lifestyle
why: Optical figures for a dim-light jumping spider would ground the view's dim-light fade.

authors: Blest AD, McIntyre PD, Carter M
title: A re-examination of the principal retinae of Phidippus johnsoni and Plexippus validus (Araneae: Salticidae): implications for optical modelling
why: The 0.13 degree spacing in Phidippus, which sets the gaze strip's sharpness, is known here only through Harland et al. 2012.

title: Retinal mosaics of the principal eyes of jumping spiders (Salticidae) in some neotropical habitats: optical trade-offs between sizes and habitat illuminances
why: Receptor spacings across several genera and light habitats would allow sharpness to vary by genus.

title: Retinal mosaics of the principal eyes of some jumping spiders (Salticidae: Araneae): adaptations for high visual acuity
why: More acuity figures for the gaze strip by genus.

title: Behavioural evidence of UV sensitivity in jumping spiders (Araneae: Salticidae)
why: Behavioural ultraviolet tests would confirm or correct the ultraviolet part of the colour row.

authors: Li J, Zhang Z, Liu F, Liu Q, Gan W, Chen J, Lim MLM, Li D
title: UVB-based mate-choice cues used by females of the jumping spider Phintella vittata
why: The ultraviolet B result is known here only through Land and Nilsson 2012.

title: Learning and discrimination of colored papers in jumping spiders (Araneae, Salticidae)
why: A behavioural colour test with grey papers would show whether a common dichromat tells hue from brightness; no DOI was printed on the pages that cite it (the University of Florida EDIS page IN1177 and the Australian Faunal Directory).

authors: Bednarski JV, Taylor PW, Jakob EM
title: Optical cues used in predation by jumping spiders, Phidippus audax (Araneae, Salticidae)
why: Which features of prey the Bold Jumping Spider attends to would refine the salience weights.

title: Hyperacute motion detection by the lateral eyes of jumping spiders
why: The size of the smallest detectable displacement would set how fine the surround's motion detector should be.

authors: Koyanagi M, Nagata T, Katoh K, Yamashita S, Tokunaga F
title: Molecular evolution of arthropod color vision deduced from multiple opsin genes of jumping spiders
why: Opsin genes would show which colour classes jumping spiders can build.

title: Movements of the eyes (chapter in Animal Eyes, second edition)
why: The library copy read here stopped at page 65; this chapter covers scanning retinas, including jumping spiders'.

title: Neurobiology of Arachnids: chapters V (Blest, retinae), VI (Yamashita, photoreceptor cells) and XIII (Forster, target discrimination)
why: The library copy read here stops inside chapter IV; these chapters hold the retinal, photoreceptor and target-discrimination evidence.

authors: Elias DO, Hebets EA, Hoy RR, Mason AC
title: Seismic signals are crucial for male mating success in a visual specialist jumping spider (Araneae: Salticidae)
why: Would fill out the vibration part of the senses the picture leaves out.

title: The distances at which a primitive jumping spider, Portia fimbriata, makes visual discriminations
why: Free on the journal's site, which refused this machine; discrimination distances for Portia.

title: Neurobiology and vision of jumping spiders (Araneae: Salticidae)
why: An open 81-page review whose host refused this machine; it may gather figures this sheet lacks.

authors: Aguilar-Argüello SO, Taylor AH, Nelson XJ
title: Jumping spiders do not seem fooled by texture gradient illusions
why: Bears on which depth cues jumping spiders use.
